extracted.intended_audience: patent applicants, patent attorneys/agents, and patent examiners (practitioners preparing or reviewing appeal briefs and examiner’s answers)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for preparing, filing, and responding to appeal briefs, amendments, affidavits/evidence, and examiner’s answers in USPTO patent appeals under 37 CFR Part 41 (MPEP §§1205–1207).

rubrics_metrics.name: Related appeals/related cases statement
rubrics_metrics.description: Statement identifying related appeals, interferences, or trials that are related to, directly affect or be directly affected by or have a bearing on the Board’s decision in the pending appeal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If there are no such related cases, the appellant is not required to include the statement; if appellant has not included the statement, the Office may assume there are no such related cases. The rule does not require Appellant to provide copies of decisions in related cases.

rubrics_metrics.name: Summary of claimed subject matter
rubrics_metrics.description: A concise explanation of the subject matter defined in each of the rejected independent claims, referring to the specification in the Record by page and line number or by paragraph number, and to the drawing, if any, by reference characters.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For each rejected independent claim, and for each dependent claim argued separately, if the claim contains a means-plus-function or step-plus-function recitation as permitted by 35 U.S.C. 112(f), the concise explanation must identify the structure, material, or acts described in the specification in the Record as corresponding to each claimed function with reference to the specification by page/line or paragraph number and drawing reference characters. Reference to the patent application publication does not satisfy this requirement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Argument requirement (content and citations)
rubrics_metrics.description: Arguments with respect to each ground of rejection and the basis therefor, including citations of statutes, regulations, authorities and parts of the Record relied on.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Arguments shall explain why the examiner erred as to each ground of rejection contested by appellant. A statement which merely points out what a claim recites will not be considered an argument for patentability. See Ex parte Frye and In re Jung for examples. 37 CFR 41.37(c)(1)(iv) emphasizes inclusion of all arguments and authorities in the brief; otherwise they will be refused consideration by the Board for the present appeal.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inclusion of all arguments and authorities in brief
rubrics_metrics.description: All arguments and authorities which an appellant wishes the Board to consider for purposes of the present appeal should be included in the appeal brief.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Arguments not presented in the briefs and made for the first time at the oral hearing are not normally entitled to consideration except as provided in 37 CFR 41.47. The rule is limited to 'the present appeal' and does not preclude filing a supplemental brief or document if new authority becomes available after filing (e.g., a pertinent decision that was not published until after the brief was filed).

rubrics_metrics.name: Separate heading per ground of rejection
rubrics_metrics.description: Each ground of rejection must be argued under a separate heading that clearly identifies the ground of rejection being contested.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For grounds applying to two or more claims, claims may be argued separately, as a group, or as a subgroup. When grouped, the Board may select a single claim and decide the appeal as to the group based on that claim alone. Failure to separately argue claims that appellant has grouped together constitutes a waiver of any argument that the Board must consider patentability of any grouped claim separately. Under each heading identifying the ground being contested, any claim(s) argued separately or as a subgroup shall be placed under a separate subheading that identifies the claim(s) by number.

rubrics_metrics.name: Claims appendix content and format
rubrics_metrics.description: An appendix containing a copy of the claims involved in the appeal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The copy should be a clean copy and should not include markings such as brackets or underlining except for claims in a reissue application and reexamination proceedings (see MPEP §1454 and relevant CFRs). The copy of the claims should be double-spaced and the appendix should start on a new page. 37 CFR 41.37(c)(1) specifies minimum requirements; a brief may optionally include list of references, table of contents, table of cases, copies of evidence entered by the examiner and relied upon in the brief, etc., but must include the required items (i) to (v) in order and must not include prohibited material.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibition on including non‑admitted amendments or new evidence in brief
rubrics_metrics.description: A brief shall not include any new or non-admitted amendment, affidavit, or other evidence.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: 37 CFR 41.37(c)(2) prohibits inclusion of non-admitted materials in the brief. If appellant wishes to seek review of an examiner’s refusal to admit an amendment, affidavit, or evidence, such review is by petition to the Director under 37 CFR 1.181. The time for filing the petition is based on the date the examiner refused to enter the material, not the date the brief was filed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Required items and order for a compliant appeal brief
rubrics_metrics.description: A compliant appeal brief should include items (i) to (v) in the order set forth by 37 CFR 41.37(c)(1).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example format and content (each starting on a separate page) includes: (A) Identification page (applicant name(s), application number, filing date, title of invention, name of examiner, art unit, title of the paper), (B) Table of Contents, (C) Real party in interest page(s), (D) Related appeals/interferences/trials page(s), (E) Summary of claimed subject matter, (F) Argument, (G) Claims appendix.

rubrics_metrics.name: Brief must be directed to claims and record as of time of appeal
rubrics_metrics.description: The brief must be directed to the claims and to the record of the case as they appeared at the time of the appeal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If appellant wishes to remove claims from consideration on appeal, an amendment to cancel the claims must be submitted (see 37 CFR 41.31(c) and 41.33). An appellant may choose not to present arguments or rely upon particular evidence for certain claim rejections, but such arguments and evidence are waived for purposes of the appeal and the Board may summarily sustain any grounds of rejection not argued.

rubrics_metrics.name: Patent Appeal Center (PAC) compliance review and correction procedure
rubrics_metrics.description: Timely filed briefs are referred to the Patent Appeal Center for determination of compliance with 37 CFR 41.37; determination is completed in approximately one month.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If brief is compliant or contains only minor informalities, PAC accepts and forwards to examiner. If non-compliant, PAC sends notice requiring a corrected brief; appellant must file corrected brief within time set in notice or appeal may be dismissed. If appellant disagrees with noncompliance holding, a petition under 37 CFR 41.3 may be filed (filing the petition does not toll the time for reply). Once accepted by the Board as compliant, the brief will not later be held defective by the PAC or the examiner; PAC will correspond directly with appellant on non-compliant brief issues; examiners are not required to review briefs for compliance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Entry and treatment of amendments after notice of appeal but before brief
rubrics_metrics.description: Amendments filed after the date of filing an appeal and prior to filing a brief may be admitted as provided in 37 CFR 1.116.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A new amendment must be submitted in a separate paper. Entry of an amendment in an application on appeal is not a matter of right and is governed by 37 CFR 41.33. Amendments filed after the filing of a notice of appeal but prior to a brief may be admitted only to (A) cancel claims (not affecting scope of other pending claims), (B) comply with form requirements expressly set forth in a previous action, (C) present rejected claims in better form for consideration on appeal, or (D) amend the specification or claims upon a showing of good and sufficient reasons why necessary and not earlier presented (see 37 CFR 41.33(a)). If examiner denies entry, use form PTOL-303 to notify applicant.

rubrics_metrics.name: Amendments permitted after filing brief
rubrics_metrics.description: Amendments filed on or after the date of filing a brief may be admitted only in limited circumstances.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Per 37 CFR 41.33(b), admitted amendments after filing a brief may be: (1) to cancel claims where cancellation does not affect scope of other pending claims; or (2) to rewrite dependent claims into independent form. 37 CFR 41.37(c)(2) provides that a brief shall not include any non-admitted amendment; any amendment filed at same time as brief must be submitted in a separate paper. Amendments filed after jurisdiction passes to the Board are not considered prior to expiration of time set in 37 CFR 90.3 unless remanded by the Board.

rubrics_metrics.name: Standards for admitting affidavits or other evidence after appeal
rubrics_metrics.description: Affidavits or other evidence filed after the date of filing a notice of appeal but prior to filing a brief may be admitted only under specific conditions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Admittance requires the examiner to determine that (A) the affidavit or other evidence overcomes all rejections under appeal; and (B) a showing of good and sufficient reasons why the affidavit/evidence is necessary and was not earlier presented has been made. All other affidavits/evidence filed after the date of filing an appeal will not be admitted except as permitted by §§41.39(b)(1), 41.50(a)(2)(i), and 41.50(b)(1). If examiner denies entry, use form PTOL-303 to notify applicant. If evidence would clearly place the application in condition for allowance, the examiner may enter it and allow the application.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rewriting dependent claims into independent form (what it includes)
rubrics_metrics.description: Rewriting dependent claims into independent form as permitted under 37 CFR 41.33(b)(2) is defined.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Includes: (A) rewriting a dependent claim in independent form by adding thereto the limitations of the parent claim(s); and (B) rewriting an independent claim to incorporate all subject matter of a dependent claim, canceling the dependent claim and changing dependencies of claims that depended from the now-canceled dependent claim to the amended independent claim.

rubrics_metrics.name: Information Disclosure Statements filed after notice of appeal
rubrics_metrics.description: Information Disclosure Statements (IDS) submitted after the date of a notice of appeal are normally held in abeyance pending a decision on the appeal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consideration of IDS is based on MPEP § 609 and 37 CFR 1.97 and 1.98 and not on 37 CFR 41.33.

rubrics_metrics.name: Examiner’s answer: incorporation and new grounds
rubrics_metrics.description: An examiner’s answer is deemed to incorporate all grounds of rejection set forth in the Office action from which the appeal is taken (as modified), unless expressly indicated withdrawn; the examiner’s answer may include a new ground of rejection.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Any rejection that relies upon any evidence not relied upon in the Office action shall be designated a new ground of rejection. Examiner must obtain approval of the Director (delegated to TC Directors/designees) to furnish an answer that includes a new ground of rejection. If answer contains a new ground, appellant has two months to either (1) reopen prosecution (request withdrawal of the appeal by filing a reply under §1.111 with or without amendment or submission of affidavits/evidence relevant to the new ground) or (2) maintain the appeal by filing a reply brief addressing the new ground (no amendments/affidavits/evidence may accompany such reply brief).

rubrics_metrics.name: Examiner’s answer content and organization
rubrics_metrics.description: The examiner’s answer should include, under appropriate headings and in the order indicated, items such as Grounds of Rejection to be Reviewed on Appeal and Response to Argument.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Grounds of Rejection to be Reviewed on Appeal must state every ground maintained and list withdrawn rejections under 'WITHDRAWN REJECTIONS' and new grounds under 'NEW GROUNDS OF REJECTION' with statutory references, prior art relied upon, and claim numbers. Response to Argument must state whether examiner disagrees with each of appellant’s arguments and explain reasons, using headings and subheadings paralleling those in the appellant’s brief. Examiner should furnish the written answer within 2 months after receipt of the brief.

rubrics_metrics.name: Examiner’s handling of amendments/after-final matters before preparing answer
rubrics_metrics.description: Before preparing the examiner’s answer, the examiner must ensure each after-final amendment or evidence has been indicated as entered or not-entered and an advisory action entered.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The examiner should identify how individual rejections set forth in the final rejection would be used to reject added or amended claims where amendment under 37 CFR 1.116 or 41.33 would be entered for appeal purposes. If an after-final amendment/evidence is not indicated as entered/not-entered and acted upon in an advisory action, the Board may remand the application.

rubrics_metrics.name: Treatment of affidavits/declarations/exhibits and non‑entered materials
rubrics_metrics.description: Examiners should treat affidavits, declarations, or exhibits filed with the notice of appeal in accordance with 37 CFR 1.116; if such material was refused entry, the examiner should not comment on it in the examiner’s answer.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: It would be improper for appellant to rely on an affidavit/declaration/exhibit not entered in the Record in an appeal brief. If appellant has grounds for challenging non-entry, they should file a timely petition under 37 CFR 1.181 seeking supervisory review of the non-entry. Any affidavits/declarations swearing behind a reference should be clearly identified by the examiner as being considered under 37 CFR 1.131.

rubrics_metrics.name: Foreign language documents relied upon by examiner
rubrics_metrics.description: If a document relied upon by the examiner in support of a rejection is in a language other than English, a translation must be obtained.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Translation may be a machine translation or an English equivalent so the record is clear as to the precise facts relied upon. See MPEP § 2120 for reliance upon abstracts and foreign language documents in support of a rejection.

rubrics_metrics.name: Presumption that all rejected claims are on appeal
rubrics_metrics.description: The Board will presume that all rejected claims are on appeal except for any claims subsequently canceled by amendment; examiner should treat all pending, rejected claims as being on appeal and maintain rejections unless overcome.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In situations where appellant requests to hold a rejection in abeyance or did not present any argument on a rejection, the examiner should maintain the rejection in the examiner’s answer and identify that appellant has not argued it in the appeal brief.

rubrics_metrics.name: Withdrawal of rejections and noting changes of status
rubrics_metrics.description: If examiner withdraws any rejections, they should be listed under 'WITHDRAWN REJECTIONS' and the answer should note any change of status of independent or dependent claims.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the examiner withdraws all rejections of an independent claim while maintaining rejections of other claims, note the change of status. If a dependent claim’s rejections are withdrawn, applicant may file an amendment to rewrite dependent claims in independent form under 37 CFR 41.33(b)(2) within time set by 37 CFR 90.3. Examiner should expressly withdraw any rejections not adhered to in the 'WITHDRAWN REJECTIONS' subsection.

rubrics_metrics.name: New grounds of rejection procedure and approval
rubrics_metrics.description: A new ground of rejection is permitted in an examiner’s answer but must be approved and signed by the Director (or designee) and properly designated as 'NEW GROUNDS OF REJECTION'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For each new ground, a complete explanation supporting the rejection must be provided with a proper reference to the applicable statute, prior art references relied upon, and claim numbers. Approval authority is delegated to Technology Center Directors or designees; the answer must include signature of TC Director/designee to indicate approval.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appeal conference requirement and participants
rubrics_metrics.description: An appeal conference is mandatory in all cases in which an acceptable brief has been filed (with limited exceptions where SPE approves not holding conference).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Participants should include (1) the examiner preparing the examiner’s answer, (2) a supervisory patent examiner (SPE), and (3) another experienced examiner (conferee). Consideration should be given to dropping cumulative art rejections and eliminating technical rejections of doubtful value. The examiner responsible for preparing the answer should weigh arguments presented; if the rejection(s) are maintained, that examiner will prepare the examiner’s answer. The examiner's answer should include the word 'Conferees:' followed by typed/printed names of the other two participants and their initials to make the record clear that an appeal conference has been held. Patent Appeal Center will review examiner’s answer for indication that an appeal conference was held and may return the application for corrective action if not.

rubrics_metrics.name: Routing and supervisory handling of significant examiner answers
rubrics_metrics.description: If an examiner’s answer is believed to contain a new interpretation or application of existing patent law, it should be forwarded to the TC Director with an explanatory memorandum for consideration and possibly to the Office of the Deputy Commissioner for Patent Examination Policy.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If approved by the TC Director, the examiner’s answer should be forwarded for final approval by the Office of the Deputy Commissioner for Patent Examination Policy (see MPEP § 1003).

rubrics_metrics.name: Timeliness and procedural effects of examiner’s answer mailing date
rubrics_metrics.description: The mailing date of the examiner’s answer begins the period for filing a reply brief and the time for appellants to request an oral hearing; examiner should furnish answer within 2 months after receipt of the brief.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: While 37 CFR 41.39(a) states examiner 'may' furnish a written answer, current procedures do not permit appeal to proceed to the Board without an examiner’s answer. Extensions of time under §1.136(a) are not applicable to the time period set forth in this section; see §1.136(b) for extensions to reply for patent applications and §1.550(c) for ex parte reexamination proceedings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Form paragraphs and standardized templates for examiner’s answer
rubrics_metrics.description: Form paragraphs and a suggested form for the examiner’s answer are provided for consistency and compliance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples include form ¶12.249 (Examiner’s Answer Cover Sheet) and ¶12.254 (Grounds of Rejection to be Reviewed on Appeal). The form specifies where to insert application number, filing date, appellant name(s), representative, and brief filing date, and instructions for following form paragraphs.
